objective: Group opaque items under safe observed property keys with an honest optional-group return type.

relevanceRationale.presentDay: PropertyKey constraints and Partial mapped records remain current TypeScript concepts.
relevanceRationale.practicalUtility: Safe dynamic grouping is practical data processing.
relevanceRationale.transferable: Observed versus possible keys, prototype ownership and numeric/Symbol key semantics transfer to other dictionaries.
relevanceRationale.audienceFit: Explicit optional groups make the intermediate generic/record lesson self-contained.
relevanceRationale.riskOutcome: Inherited prototype functions masquerading as arrays and unsafe absent-group typing cause real false failures.

defects: All old plain-object boards failed for prototype-like group keys.
Required Record<K,T[]> promised groups for every possible K even on empty input.
Explanation confused possible callback keys with actually observed keys.
Old tests accepted the unsafe dictionary and its unsound required-group type.
rationale: Rewrite prompt/starter/scaffold/hints/steps and all boards to Partial<Record<K,T[]>> with prototype-safe empty dictionaries. Correct three public type expectations and add a missing-group rejection plus a symbol-key optional lookup. Define one ordered single-argument callback call, exact thrown-value propagation, observed own keys only, missing keys undefined, numeric string coercion and Symbol identity. Nineteen cohort runtime checks include prototype names and missing inherited names, numeric/string/signed-zero aliases, distinct Symbols, callback arity, independent groups and1000 values. The final accepted alternative uses a canonical-key Map and null-prototype output with the corrected Partial type; the baseline Record/ordinary-own-key alternative belongs to the old contract and is not falsely carried forward. Raw legacy output independently fails at runtime with a prototype-key push error and fails the new absent-group type assertion. Installed TypeScript5.9.3 Object.groupBy declarations likewise use Partial; official5.4 notes explain optional groups. Target linear own grouping work/output excluding callback work under bounded key operations.

objective: Fold generic values with a linear loop and exact two-argument callback/accumulator identity semantics.

defects: Exact callback arity/count/order and opaque accumulator lifetime were unstated.
Senior recursively copied rest arrays, producing quadratic copying rather than the requested loop.
Direct native reduce(step,initial) passed all old callbacks that ignored extra arguments.
rationale: Retain reference and align junior/senior to indexed loops, with original for-of as valid iterative alternative. Define stable dense frozen input through1000 and exactly two callback arguments, exact initial/returned references, no wrapper coercion/await/calls on opaque values, no calls when empty and exact thrown-value propagation. Callback-owned accumulator mutation is allowed. Cases inspect evolving accumulator identity and arguments.length, empty function/Symbol/undefined initial values, thrown-marker stop order and a1000-value mutable accumulator without input changes. Add a static function-U preservation proof. Target linear wrapper work/constant wrapper state excluding callback work/allocated state. Syntax is a teaching objective; finite grading is not a proof about every possible source implementation.
